name: Keyword alerts from public Telegram channels to your Telegram chat

parameters.content:
## Keyword alerts from public Telegram channels to your Telegram chat

### How it works
Every hour this workflow reads the public Telegram channels you list and sends you a Telegram message for each new post that mentions one of your keywords: channel, matched keyword, the first 600 characters, view count, time and link. Good for watching exchange announcement channels for listings, news channels for a company name, or competitors' channels.

It uses the [Telegram Channel Scraper](https://apify.com/ninoventures/telegram-channel-scraper) actor on Apify. No Telegram account or phone number is needed for reading; it uses the public t.me/s preview. With "only new posts" on, each run returns only posts published after the previous run. The first run sends the latest matches, up to the alert limit.

### Setup
1. Create an Apify account and copy your API token.
2. In **Fetch new matching posts**, create a Header Auth credential: name `Authorization`, value `Bearer YOUR_TOKEN`.
3. Create a bot with @BotFather, add its token as a Telegram credential in **Send alert to Telegram**, then send your bot a message.
4. Put your chat ID in **Settings** (message @userinfobot to get it), plus the channels and keywords.

### Cost
$0.60 per 1,000 matching posts. Posts without a keyword match are not charged.

### Limits
Only channels with a public web preview work. Private channels and groups are skipped.

## Configure
Channels, keywords, your chat ID and the alert cap.

## Get new matching posts
Keyword matching happens in the actor, so only matches are returned and charged.

## Format and send
One message per post. Extra posts beyond the cap are counted in a final message.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ channels: $json.channels.split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean), keywords: $json.keywords.split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean), maxPostsPerChannel: 50, maxPagesPerChannel: 10, onlyNewPosts: true, monitorName: $json.monitorName }) }}
